content.text: {"label":"unknown_demand_surge","explanation":"Both queues are getting far more calls than forecast: payments +47% recently (+59% at 11:15) and general about +30%. The rise is spread evenly across every call reason rather than concentrated in a few, so no single trigger stands out. There is no logged incident to suggest an outage. The only marketing send (KYC reminder SMS, 07:30) would mainly drive account_update calls on general, so it does not explain a payments-led rise across all reasons. Supply is not the cause either: agents on phones match plan, there is only 1 absence against about 2 usual, and handle time is at or below forecast. This is a demand surge whose cause the information does not establish.","plan_name":"Absorb unexplained surge: free levers first, then overtime within budget","rationale":"Payments needs roughly 10–13 extra agents' worth of capacity. Moving agents from general is not allowed, because general is itself at 50–62% service level, below the 70% donor floor. Instead the plan stacks levers. Delaying breaks gives free capacity at the peak, and cancelling coaching recovers a modest amount for Rs 150 per session hour. Callback offers flatten queue peaks, and chat deflection for status enquiries removes simple calls at Rs 12 per chat. Overtime is staged in approval-to-arrival order. Payments: 20 offered for 12:00–14:00, about 8 accepted, about Rs 5,760; 15 offered for 14:00–16:00, about 6 accepted, about Rs 4,320. General: 10 offered for 12:00–14:00, about 4 accepted, about Rs 2,880. Expected overtime total is about Rs 12,960, within the Rs 15,000 daily budget. Volumes should be re-checked at each interval and the later offer adjusted if the surge
